messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Kruskal-Wallis
parts:
The nonparametric statistic in scanone is basically Kruskal-Wallis, but dealing with missing genotype information. See Broman (2003) Genetics 163:1169-1175 http://bit.ly/2partPDF

It's not implemented for composite interval mapping (or scantwo, for that matter). I'm not aware of such a nonparametric statistic that can handle covariates or multiple loci.

You could try converting the phenotype to normal scores (turn into ranks and then calculate the corresponding normal quantiles); use the function nqrank() in R/qtl. That tends to behave similarly to the non-parametric methods.

karl
